id_and_class.summary: Michael Tye, once a reductive physicalist, now argues that phenomenal consciousness is irreducible because it has no borderline cases: a state is either conscious or not. At the fundamental level there is ‘consciousness*’ (protoconsciousness), which transfers to complex systems that play the right functional role and represent properties. Differences in what experiences are like come from differences in what they represent, which keeps his earlier representationalism.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Irreducible On/Off Consciousness Transferred from the Fundamental

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal consciousness is an irreducible, all-or-nothing property whose basic form, consciousness*, belongs to fundamental entities.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Consciousness* passes from fundamental physical entities to complex combinations of them that meet functional and representational conditions; those combinations are conscious in the full-blooded sense.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (consciousness* is fundamental; full consciousness arises by transfer to suitably organized systems)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Experiences represent properties and property complexes, and their representational content fixes what they are like.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Differences in phenomenal character are differences in what experiences represent, as in Tye's earlier PANIC theory. Content can be vague (pure red or a hint of orange), but whether consciousness* is present is never vague.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Fundamental entities bearing consciousness*, and complex systems with the right functional roles and representational contents.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Philosophical reasoning about the structure of experience, especially the absence of borderline cases.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Consciousness* at the base level plus representational content at the level of complex systems.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Transfer of consciousness* from fundamental entities to combinations that play the right functional role and represent properties.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness* is present in fundamental entities; full consciousness exists only in complex systems meeting the functional and representational conditions.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Tye claims the transfer account gives a straightforward solution to panpsychism's combination problem, since only qualifying combinations become conscious.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Representation is central: what a conscious state represents determines its phenomenal character.
core_claims_and_evidence: Phenomenal consciousness has no borderline cases; it is an on/off matter.
The best explanation for that absence of borderline cases is that phenomenal consciousness is irreducible.
No plausible, non-arbitrary reductive physical candidate exists for an on/off property, so Tye drops his earlier contingent reductive physicalism.
The view is his original PANIC theory with consciousness* added.

empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Tye says the conversion bothered him for a long time. The functional and representational conditions that trigger transfer are named but not spelled out.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The view keeps representationalism and functional roles from his physicalist period while making consciousness itself irreducible.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since any combination with the right functional role and representations becomes conscious, it follows from the view that an artificial system meeting those conditions would be too.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Tye's Irreducible Consciousness* (Landscape of Consciousness), Michael Tye
